headline: Lawrence woman indicted after husband's death in alleged caretaker neglect, MassHealth fraud case
dek: Judit Diaz de Vargas faces involuntary manslaughter, caretaker-neglect and fraud charges after prosecutors said she billed MassHealth while caring for her husband.
body: A Lawrence woman has been indicted on involuntary manslaughter, caretaker-neglect and MassHealth fraud charges after the death of her husband, Massachusetts Attorney General Andrea Campbell's office announced Sept. 25.

The Essex County grand jury indictment charges Judit Diaz de Vargas, 49, with involuntary manslaughter, caretaker neglect causing serious bodily injury, caretaker neglect involving an elder, Medicaid false claims and larceny by false pretenses over $1,200. She was arraigned in Essex Superior Court on Sept. 25, where bail was set at $15,000.

Prosecutors allege that Diaz de Vargas applied in April 2023 to become her husband's MassHealth personal care attendant and identified herself as his ex-daughter-in-law after being told that spouses could not serve as PCAs under program rules. The attorney general's office said MassHealth paid about $135,000 based on timesheets she submitted between April 2023 and November 2025.

The attorney general's office alleges that the husband was admitted to Lawrence General Hospital in October 2025 with more than 10 pressure wounds, at least eight of them unstageable, and extreme emaciation. He died four days later from sepsis caused by infections in necrotic wounds, according to the office.

The case began after the hospital contacted an adult protective services agency, which referred the matter to the attorney general's Medicaid Fraud Division. Medical records and interviews with medical workers and family members led investigators to allege that the wounds would not have progressed to that condition if proper care had been provided.

The judge barred Diaz de Vargas from working with the PCA or other MassHealth programs, working or volunteering with older or disabled people, and traveling outside Massachusetts without permission. The charges are allegations, and she is presumed innocent unless proven guilty in court. Lawrence police, Massachusetts State Police assigned to the Essex County District Attorney's Office, the Essex County District Attorney's Office and the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Office of Inspector General assisted the investigation.
author: NorthEast News Desk
